simulate.description: Run one ngspice batch simulation (ngspice -b) of a deck. Inputs: deck (path relative to the design root; the deck holds the circuit, the analyses and a .control block), libs (optional list of {path, section}; each becomes a .lib line before the deck, for example a PDK corner; $PDK_ROOT is expanded), measurements (optional {name: unit}). A measurement is read from a 'name = value' line in the ngspice output, so use meas or print in the .control block with the same name. A wanted name that ngspice does not print is reported as missing. params (optional {name: number or string}) and temp_c (optional number) become .param and .temp lines after the deck, so they replace the deck's values. A sweep bench prints one line per point, 'ROW <sweep>=<v> <name>=<value> ...' (echo in a foreach loop); the response then has <name>.min and <name>.max with 'at', the sweep point, and work/sweep.json has the table. A point without a value makes .min and .max failed. Files that the deck writes (for example with wrdata) go to the work directory of the experiment and are hashed. The response has a warning for each simulator option that adds elements to the circuit (rshunt, cshunt, a gmin above 1e-12), with its file and line.

operating_point.description: Find the DC operating point of each MOS device of a testbench, and whether it is in saturation. Inputs: deck and libs, as for simulate; technology (optional, the name of a technology pack; the default is the pack for $PDK). The adapter removes the .control blocks, the analyses and the .meas lines of the deck, and runs 'op' at the DC values of the sources in the netlist. To check one condition (for example one input common-mode voltage or one corner), set the DC values and the libs for that condition. The response has, for each MOS device, the measurements <device>.vgs, .vth, .vds, .vdsat, .id, .gm, .gds, .vov (|vgs| - |vth|) and .sat_margin (|vds| - |vdsat|), all as magnitudes for PMOS too, and a warning for each device in triode (sat_margin < 0) or subthreshold (vov < 0). work/operating_point.json has the region of each device. Use it to find why a design fails, before you change a size. Run it at the condition that fails (the corner in libs and the DC values of the failing point, for example the end of an input range), not only at the nominal condition: a device can be in saturation at tt and in triode at ss.

lint.description: Check netlists without a simulation. Inputs: files (list of netlist paths relative to the design root). The response has the same option warnings as simulate, for each file and the files that it includes from the design root.

check_design.description: Check a design netlist against its design contract. It runs no simulation: it reads the netlist in the ngspice form with the ngspice.* facts of the technology pack (devices, size unit, passive area). Inputs: file (relative to the design root), subckt, pins (in order), elements (allowed kinds, "mos", "r", "c"; default all), devices (the allowed devices of the technology pack; default all; a name that the pack does not have fails the run), limits ({r_ohm, c_f}, the maximum value of one R or C), technology (optional; the default is the pack for $PDK). Rules: the file holds only .subckt blocks without parameters. In a block, an X line instantiates a MOS device of the technology pack that devices allows (with plain-number sizes in the size unit of the pack, at or above the minimum) or another block of the file; R and C lines have 4 fields and a plain positive value. Sources, M lines, .model, .include, .lib, .param, .option and {expressions} are errors. The response status is completed also when the design has errors; each error is an error diagnostic with its file and line. Measurements: design_errors (the number of errors), gate_area_um2 (sum of W x L x m of all MOS devices, hierarchy expanded), passive_area_um2 (the area of the R and C, hierarchy expanded: R x w_min^2 / R_sheet and C / density, with the facts of $PDK in ngspice.passives of the technology pack), area_um2 (gate_area_um2 + passive_area_um2), mos_count. Without area facts for an R or C, passive_area_um2 and area_um2 are failed, with a warning. Put a limit on an area as a requirement on its measurement. work/design.json has the errors and the elements.

probe_devices.description: Device-class probe: one small DC deck per device class of the technology pack (section device_probe.<pdk>: a library per simulator and the netlist lines of each class, with a voltage source vprobe). Inputs: pdk (default $PDK), technology (optional pack name), classes (optional list; default every class), timeout_s (per class, default 60). Method: ngspice -b with op and print i(vprobe); the .spiceinit of the kit loads the OSDI models. One row per class: simulates (the DC current of vprobe is a finite number), parses (the netlist was read, but the analysis gave no value), fails (the netlist was not read: a model gap or an unknown subcircuit or model, with the reason and the file and line) or not run (timeout). Fidelity warnings (ignored model parameters) are listed per row. Outputs: work/probe.json (role probe, schema simra.device_probe/0) and work/probe/<class>.cir and .log. Measurements: classes_total, classes_simulates, classes_parses, classes_fails, classes_not_run. The response is completed when the probe ran, also when classes fail. The kernel merges the probes of the simulators into one table (simra probe).

assemble_dc.description: DC operating point of a large deck (a whole chip of blocks) from the operating points of its parts, by clamp homotopy. Inputs: deck, libs, params, temp_c (as simulate); seeds (required: list of {file, from_prefix, to_prefix, only_prefix}; a file is {"v(node)": volts} or {"nodes": {...}}, as an op of a block testbench or the dc_point.json of an earlier assembly; from_prefix/to_prefix map the testbench names to the deck names, for example x1. to xcore.xif.; later seeds win); phases (optional: list of node-name prefix lists, released in this order; nodes in no phase are released after them); decades (default 12); steps (per phase, default 50); solver (sparse, the ngspice default, or klu); options (one line of ngspice options, for example reltol=1e-3 itl1=1000); free_op (default true); free_op_timeout_s (default 2 x the time of the clamp sweep, at least 300 s); accept_clamp_end (default false: with true, a free op that fails or passes its time limit gives the end of the clamp sweep as the point, with a warning, and the run is completed); currents (voltage source names). Method: each seeded node gets a clamp current g (V - V_seed); a .dc sweep takes g from 1 S to 10^-decades S, one phase after the other, and each point starts from the point before; then a free op without clamps with .nodeset from the end of the sweep. Outputs: work/dc_point.json (role dc_point, the node voltages of the free op, or of the clamp end; usable as a seed), work/clamp_end.json (role clamp_end, the end of the clamp sweep with the residual clamp; usable as a seed), work/assemble.json, clamp.cir/clamp.raw, free.cir/free.raw/free.log. Measurements: nodes_seeded, clamp_points_total, clamp_points_done, clamp_x_last, clamp_reached_end, free_op_converged, free_op_max_dv_v, seeds_not_in_circuit, clamp_sweep_s, i_<source>_a (from the free op, or from the clamp end). The response is failed when the sweep stops (the error names the phase), or when the free op does not converge in its time limit and accept_clamp_end is false.

oscillator.description: Steady-state frequency, amplitude and phase noise of an oscillator by the impulse sensitivity function (ISF), from ngspice transients. Inputs: deck, libs, params, temp_c (as simulate; the deck must start to oscillate by itself, for example with a short current kick); output ({p, n}: the output is v(p) - v(n), or v(p)); tstep_s (fixed time step), settle_s (start-up time), ref_stop_s (end of the reference run, default 1.25 settle_s); output_multiplier (default 1; L at the output of an ideal frequency multiplier adds 20 log10 of it); isf (optional: phases (default 32), window_periods (default [35, 45]), dq_c (default 2e-17), dl_vs (default 2e-16), pulse_s (default T/160), offsets_hz (default [1e5, 1e6, 1e7]), parallel (default all CPUs of the job), t0_s (optional: the phase origin, between settle_s and ref_stop_s; default the first rising zero crossing after settle_s), devices (optional: list of {name, lines (the device alone, for example 'x1 c b 0 0 npn13G2 Nx=2'), sweep [[node, from, to, step], [node, from, to, step]] (a 2-D dc sweep of two node voltages), axes (two vectors of the table deck, for example the internal vbe and vbc), at (the same two vectors in the oscillator deck), currents {name: vector of the table deck}}: a DC conduction table of the device, interpolated at the transient axis values of each phase; the model lines of the deck are copied into the table deck), sources: list of {name, nodes: 'n+ n-', psd_a2_hz (a number, or a list with one PSD per phase) or shot ({device, current}: the conduction current of a device table, S = 2 q |i| at each phase; or a vector of the reference run, which must be a conduction current: in a transient the terminal currents of a bipolar model and @q[ib] of VBIC include charge currents), flicker (optional {device, current, kf, af, bf}: S = kf |i|^af / df^bf by the DC term of the ISF), mult} or {name, vsource (a voltage source of value 0 in series), psd_v2_hz, mult}). Method: a reference transient gives f0 and the amplitude after settle_s; for each source and phase, two runs inject +q and -q with a short triangle pulse, and the shift of the output zero crossings in the window gives the ISF in s/C (s/(V s) for a series source); L(df) = mult x 1/2 (f0/df)^2 x mean(ISF^2 S) per source, summed. Flicker: L = mult x 1/2 (f0/df)^2 x mean(ISF x |i|^(af/2))^2 x kf / df^bf. Not included: AM-to-PM conversion after the oscillator. Outputs: work/oscillator.json (role oscillator: f0, amplitude, the ISF, PSD and L of each source, the total), ref.cir, ngspice.log; the logs of failed ISF runs. Measurements: f0_hz, f_out_hz, amplitude_v, period_spread_rel (a warning above 1e-3: not in steady state), l_<offset>_hz_dbc (for example l_1e+06_hz_dbc; with flicker included), l_white_<offset>_hz_dbc (when a source has flicker). The response is failed when the circuit does not oscillate or an ISF run fails.
